subject: Food Science
title: Enzymatic Browning
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Enzymatic Browning.

hook.text: Cut an apple and it turns brown in minutes. No bacteria—the apple's own enzymes are destroying it from within.

buildup.text: Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) reacts with oxygen when cell walls are damaged. It creates brown melanin pigments.

discovery.text: Blanching—briefly boiling vegetables—deactivates PPO with heat. That's why frozen vegetables stay green for months.

twist.text: Arctic Apples were genetically engineered to silence PPO genes. They don't brown—ever. Some consumers object.

climax.text: Lemon juice, citric acid, and ascorbic acid slow browning by lowering pH and scavenging oxygen—simple kitchen tricks.

punchline.text: The apple browns itself. Stop the enzyme and you stop the clock.

quiz.question: What causes a cut apple to turn brown?
options: Polyphenol oxidase reacting with oxygen after cell damage
